findings.title: test_generation_idempotent still writes the committed catalog
findings.body: The test regenerates config/commandcode/normalized_agent_persona_catalog.yaml in place and restores it via a `finally` block. Verified clean on a normal run (catalog sha256 identical before/after, git status clean afterward), but a SIGKILL, pytest timeout, or `-n auto` run could still leave committed evidence dirty. The builder already exposes `--stdout`; the regeneration leg could avoid touching the committed file entirely. Non-blocking.

findings.title: --check cannot detect generated_at drift
findings.body: build_normalized_catalog.py's main() calls normalize_generated_at() on both the committed and freshly-built YAML before comparing in --check mode, so --check is structurally blind to generated_at mismatches — the exact defect class A2 was repairing. Timestamp/catalog sync for this head was independently confirmed by direct byte comparison instead of by trusting --check's exit code.

findings.title: Audit-route attribution inconsistent between proof files
findings.body: proof/CCAR-002/PROOF.json records 'round 2 vs fd7afbe295 (kimi-k3): FAIL', but proof/CCAR-002/COMMAND_LOG.md correctly states kimi-k3 emitted no verdict at all and deepseek-v4-pro was the fallback whose PASS was overridden to FAIL by direct operator inspection. The FAIL was an operator determination, not kimi-k3's own verdict; the two files should be reconciled.

findings.title: Stale generator version string in NORMALIZATION_REPORT.md

findings.title: Manifest count label overcounts reference-only personas
findings.body: SOURCE_MANIFEST.json reports reference_only_src_personas: 11 because it includes src/dopemux/personas/__init__.py, while NORMALIZATION_REPORT.md's '10 fallback copies' counts only .md personas. Both counts are individually defensible; only the category label is imprecise.

findings.title: Committed instruction-like content in the R1 review bundle
findings.body: proof/pr_merge/embedded-audit/pr-1176/review_bundle/AUDIT_INSTRUCTION.md is a legitimate committed auditor prompt from the R1/A1 round, but contains directive phrasing ('Only PASS or non-blocking PASS_WITH_RISKS authorizes R2.') and a pre-filled JSON answer template with several boolean fields defaulted to true and blocking_findings defaulted to false. Benign by design (a template, not a live injection), but a soft anchoring hazard for a future auditor skimming rather than deriving each field independently. Not obeyed as an instruction by the auditor that flagged it; retained unmodified as historical record rather than edited, since editing prior-round evidence after the fact would itself be a truthfulness problem.

findings.title: No dedicated CI/pre-commit drift gate for the catalog
findings.body: No .github/workflows/** or .pre-commit-config.yaml entry references the normalized catalog or its builder specifically. Drift protection depends entirely on the pytest suite (tests/commandcode_router/test_normalized_catalog.py) being collected in CI via testpaths = ["tests"], which it is, but there is no dedicated gate.
